title: c-VEP dataset from Thielen et al. (2021)
description: A code-modulated visual evoked potential (cVEP) brain-computer interface dataset from 30 healthy participants performing an offline BCI task with a calculator grid stimulus. This derivative dataset demonstrates a calibration-free approach that progressively reduces training data requirements while maintaining classification performance, ultimately achieving zero-training BCI operation through neural encoding models. The study validates the feasibility of plug-and-play BCI systems using only 8 non-invasive EEG electrodes.
methods_description: EEG data acquired at 512 Hz from 8 electrodes (Fpz, Iz, O1, O2, Oz, POz, T7, T8) using Biosemi ActiveTwo hardware with sintered Ag/AgCl active electrodes. Stimuli consisted of luminance-modulated pseudo-random Gold code sequences (126-bit, 2.1 s duration) presented on an iPad Pro at 60 Hz. Offline experiment: 30 participants completed 5 blocks of 20 trials each (100 trials total, 31.5 s per trial) using a 4×5 calculator grid. Online experiment: 11 participants used a keyboard layout with dynamic stopping rule. Preprocessing included 2-30 Hz Butterworth filtering and downsampling to 120 Hz. Classification employed template-matching with reconvolution encoding model.
